text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay B states a clear position in the introduction and repeats it in the conclusion, with three distinct reasons previewed and then developed in body paragraphs.", "quality": "Clear organizational structure", "description": "The essay follows a recognizable argumentative structure with an introduction, body paragraphs each devoted to one reason, and a conclusion that restates the position."}, {"evidence": "Essay B quotes directly from the article, e.g., \"Google cars aren't truly driverless; they still have to alert the driver to take over...\" and \"The car can handle driving functions at speeds up to 25 mph...\"", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay supports each claim with direct quotations from the source article, grounding the argument in the text."}, {"evidence": "Essay B develops each of its three reasons across a full paragraph with explanation, such as explaining why having to stay alert defeats the purpose of a driverless car.", "quality": "Reason development", "description": "Each supporting reason is elaborated with explanation and commentary rather than merely asserted."}, {"evidence": "Essay B's reasons are grounded in actual content from the article (driver alertness, liability, 25 mph speed limit) rather than imagined scenarios.", "quality": "Relevance to source", "description": "The arguments engage with the actual facts and issues presented in the article rather than fabricating unrelated scenarios."}, {"evidence": "Essay A contains numerous spelling and grammatical errors (\"driveless,\" \"strop driven,\" \"attetion,\" \"becausde\") and rambling, run-on sentences, while Essay B is largely coherent.", "quality": "Conventional control of language", "description": "The essay demonstrates greater command of spelling, grammar, and sentence structure, making the argument easier to follow."}]}
